Definition: properly, to be fresh, i.e. full (rosy, (figuratively) cheerful); to announce (glad news)
BiblicalUsage: Basar as a verb means to bring good news, to publish glad tidings. Isaiah says how beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him that brings good tidings of peace, the Spirit anoints the servant to preach good tidings to the meek, the psalm says to show forth His salvation from day to day, and Nahum says the feet of him that brings good tidings stand on the mountains.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe good news is only good because of who carries it and what it says, and Isaiah's beautiful feet belong to the messenger of peace. The gospel was good tidings before the Gospels were written, and I hold that every preacher since has only been repeating the news that God has come to save.
